answer: Sybil resistance can come from a branching rule on endorsements: a new agent joins only if its sponsors form an arborescence that does not already support a sibling, audited on a random sample each epoch. Bonds are slashed by the square of the number of clones sharing one root, so a hundred puppets under a single sponsor cost ten thousand times one bond. That delta keeps honest growth and cloned growth from ever converging, and no endorsement pool survives as a kernel others can quietly reuse. Like currents crossing an ocean, capital must travel through distinct channels, not one shared pipe.
